note: Association only. Percentiles are positions among the 24 clans with 7+ games (0 = lowest, 100 = highest). Intervals are 95%, from resampling the clan's own games. Rates with fewer than 8 cases are null ("too few"). Movement: pushing = batch label pushing (range to the nearest enemies closed while laying), kiting = batch label kiting (range opened), parked = batch label stationary; the batch label horizontal is reported as sideways and unclassified stays in the denominator. Round 5c: times are the replay clock (seconds since battle start at activation). Deaths are two scores side by side: died = a covered ship (the smoker, or a ship inside or behind the smoke) died between activation and 20 s after the smoke dispersed, distinct ships, leaving out the 9 smokes of the single-replay game laid by the team with no replay; caught = the batch smoke_deaths list. Caps come from the cap timeline, up to 60 s after dispersal: taken = owner changed to the smoking clan (of smokes where the cap was not already theirs); not lost = the enemy did not take it (of smokes inside or within 2 km of that cap, cap not the enemy's); each for the nearest cap (_n) and the contested cap (_c). Dropped from round 5b: took_pct, held_pct, deaths_per100, deaths_pg, cap_won_pg, cap_def_pg (replaced by the scores above).

styles.name: Team smoke, plenty of it
styles.description: Long-smoke destroyers (Somers, Gearing, Harugumo) lay smoke for a cruiser, usually a radar cruiser, and they lay a lot of it. Few cruisers bring their own smoke.

styles.name: Own smoke, plenty of it
styles.description: Cruisers (Svea, Jinan, Napoli) and cap-sitter destroyers (Daring, Gdansk, Shimakaze) each smoke for themselves, often parked, and there is a lot of smoke per game.

styles.name: Team smoke, little of it
styles.description: The same team-smoke habit, but few smoke ships in the lineup and few smokes per game; the first smoke comes late.

styles.name: Own smoke, little of it
styles.description: Ships smoke for themselves (Napoli exhaust, cap sitters), with few smoke destroyers and few smokes per game.

what_they_mean.pc1: Who the smoke is for. Low end: long-smoke destroyers laying smoke on or in front of a teammate, with a radar cruiser inside. High end: cruisers and cap-sitter destroyers that carry smoke and use it on themselves, more often parked or kiting.
what_they_mean.pc2: How much smoke. High end: more destroyers carrying smoke, more smokes per game, an earlier first smoke. Low end: few smoke ships, few smokes, later, more of it while pushing.

structure.one_scale_or_several: Two separate scales, not one, and not sharp types. "Adds a smoke cruiser or not" is one part of the first scale (r +0.72 with it) but who the smoke is laid for tracks it more closely (r -0.83). The second scale, how much smoke a clan brings and uses, is unrelated to the first. Together they carry 47% of the differences between clans. Clans are spread along the first scale without a break; on the second there is a gap that sets 7 low-smoke clans apart. The four named styles are the four corners of that two-scale map. They are regions with soft borders: grouping on all 17 scores at once is not stable when games are resampled.

top6_concentration.caveat: Six clans is very few; neither count is beyond what chance allows at the usual 5% level. Styles describe; they do not explain winning.
